hypotheses.claim: ConstTag client transform unconditionally wraps the @const initializer in $.derived with a plain thunk; with await this yields `$.derived(() => await ...)` — await in a non-async arrow — which fails JS parsing. Fix: when the initializer expression has await, emit `await $.save($.async_derived(async () => ...))` like VariableDeclaration does for async $derived.
evidence_refs: ConstTag.js:17-25 (create_derived with b.thunk, no await handling)
compiled_client in baseline shows `const number = $.derived(() => await Promise.resolve(5))`
VariableDeclaration.js:205-218 async $derived path uses b.thunk(expression, true) + '$.async_derived' + b.call(b.await(b.call('$.save', call)))
hypotheses.prediction: Emitting the async_derived/await form in ConstTag when node.metadata.expression.has_await will make the holdout test compile and print '5'.
hypotheses.falsifier: If the boundary callback still ends up non-async or `$.get(number)` doesn't unwrap the promise, the test will still fail — pointing to missing async body wrapping or get_value handling.

hypotheses.claim: Alternative: the bug is only in the destructuring (non-Identifier) branch of ConstTag and the Identifier branch is fine.
evidence_refs: ConstTag.js:17-25 shows Identifier branch also uses create_derived(b.thunk) with no await handling
baseline compiled output shows failure in the Identifier branch
hypotheses.prediction: Fixing only the destructuring branch would leave the holdout failing; fixing the Identifier branch fixes it.
hypotheses.falsifier: Baseline compiled output already falsifies this: the failing generated code comes from the Identifier branch.
